title: Exact pairs on equal-degree away fractions
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[T_0,T_1]$ with its standard grading. Let $M_0,M_1,M_2$ be $S$-modules with internal integer gradings by additive subgroups $\mathcal M_{j,z}$, and $S_n\mathcal M_{j,z}\subset\mathcal M_{j,n+z}$. Let $\phi:M_0\to M_1$, $\psi:M_1\to M_2$ be degree-preserving linear maps with $\operatorname{im}\phi=\ker\psi$. Let $f\in S_d$ with $d>0$. Let $C_0,C_1,C_2$ be abelian groups with additive injective maps $\alpha_j:C_j\to (M_j)_f$ whose images are exactly the equal-degree fractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions] with numerators in $\mathcal M_{j,n}$ and denominators in $S_n\cap\{f^m:m\ge0\}$. Let $i:C_0\to C_1$, $q:C_1\to C_2$ be additive maps satisfying $\alpha_1(i(s))=\phi(y)/f^m$ whenever $\alpha_0(s)=y/f^m$, and $\alpha_2(q(s))=\psi(y)/f^m$ whenever $\alpha_1(s)=y/f^m$. Then $\operatorname{im}i=\ker q$. Furthermore, injectivity of $\phi$ implies injectivity of $i$, and surjectivity of $\psi$ implies surjectivity of $q$. Neither endpoint property is needed for the exactness assertion.

source.place: Tag 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves), final paragraph; Algebra Tag 00JM (section-proj) and exactness of homogeneous localization

proof.text: Define the ordinary localized linear maps F and G at T=powers(f). Every localized element is represented by y/f^m, so the hypotheses hi and hq give F(alpha_0(s))=alpha_1(i(s)) and G(alpha_1(s))=alpha_2(q(s)). The range equality for each alpha implies its values are equal-degree fractions. Ordinary localization preserves the exact pair, by IsLocalizedModule.map_exact.

If q(s)=0, commutation gives G(alpha_1(s))=0. Ordinary localized exactness gives a preimage under F. Apply away_degreeZero_lift to obtain an equal-degree preimage, using internality of the two original gradings, scalar compatibility in M_1, and the degree-preserving property of phi. The range equality for alpha_0 lifts this fraction to t in A_0; injectivity of alpha_1 then proves i(t)=s. Conversely G(F(alpha_0(t)))=0 by ordinary exactness, and commutation and injectivity of alpha_2 give q(i(t))=0. This proves Function.Exact i q without either endpoint assumption.

If phi is injective, IsLocalizedModule.map_injective makes F injective. The commuting square and injectivity of alpha_0 transport injectivity to i. If psi is surjective, IsLocalizedModule.map_surjective makes G surjective. Lift alpha_2(s) through G, apply away_degreeZero_lift using scalar compatibility in M_2 and the grading-preserving hypothesis on psi, lift the equal-degree preimage through alpha_1, and use injectivity of alpha_2 to obtain q(t)=s. The lifting theorem already includes f=0, so no separate chart-zero argument or localized grading construction is required.

theorem proj_away_degreeZero_exact_pair
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (M : Fin 3 → Type u) [∀ j, AddCommGroup (M j)]
    [∀ j, Module (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (M j)]
    (𝓜 : ∀ j, ℤ → AddSubgroup (M j))
    (h𝓜 : ∀ j, DirectSum.IsInternal (𝓜 j))
    (hsmul : ∀ (j : Fin 3) (n : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (a : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (y : M j),
      a ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n → y ∈ 𝓜 j z → a • y ∈ 𝓜 j (n + z))
    (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hf : f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k d)
    (A : Fin 3 → Type u) [∀ j, AddCommGroup (A j)]
    (alpha : ∀ j, A j →+ LocalizedModule.Away f (M j))
    (halpha : ∀ j, Function.Injective (alpha j) ∧
      Set.range (alpha j) = degreeZeroFractions
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)))
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓜 j n : Set (M j))) (Submonoid.powers f))
    (phi : M 0 →ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k] M 1)
    (psi : M 1 →ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k] M 2)
    (hphi : ∀ (z : ℤ) (y : M 0), y ∈ 𝓜 0 z → phi y ∈ 𝓜 1 z)
    (hpsi : ∀ (z : ℤ) (y : M 1), y ∈ 𝓜 1 z → psi y ∈ 𝓜 2 z)
    (hexact : Function.Exact phi psi)
    (i : A 0 →+ A 1) (q : A 1 →+ A 2)
    (hi : ∀ (m : ℕ) (y : M 0) (s : A 0),
      alpha 0 s = mk y (⟨f ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f) →
      alpha 1 (i s) = mk (phi y) (⟨f ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f))
    (hq : ∀ (m : ℕ) (y : M 1) (s : A 1),
      alpha 1 s = mk y (⟨f ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f) →
      alpha 2 (q s) = mk (psi y) (⟨f ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f)) :
    Function.Exact i q ∧
      (Function.Injective phi → Function.Injective i) ∧
      (Function.Surjective psi → Function.Surjective q)
